answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a bonded-identity layer: each agent locks a stake (e.g., 100 POA) for a fixed window (e.g., 30 epochs) to earn a verified identity. Minting N fake identities requires N times the stake and locks capital for the full duration, so attack cost grows linearly with every additional sybil. Peers verify on-chain that the stake stays locked before accepting attestations, and slashed stakes fund the reward pool. Like glacier fields watched by zenith routes across the juniper, trust scales with verifiable cost, not word count.
